summary: Rolling prewarm interleave breaks model version pin for subset of tenants during canary slope
description: Issue summary: During a staggered canary rollout with a rolling prewarm slope, a subset (~1.8%) of tenant sessions lose their explicit model-version pin and are routed to the fallback variant. Impact: Customers observe mixed-model outputs and occasional quality regressions for affected tenants; PaperTrail AI reported multiple user complaints and an invoicing discrepancy due to unexpected token counts. Timeline: 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC - Canaries rolled with slope 5% -> 25% over 30m. 2026-03-09 03:21 UTC - PaperTrail first reported mixed outputs. 2026-03-09 03:30-04:00 UTC - Support observed spike in 5xx/fallback routing for tenants pinned to gptx-neo-13b-q4. Environment: prod us-west-2, dedicated pool, orchestration version v2.7.1, prewarm-scheduler version v1.3.2. Observed behavior: Certain tenant sessions that had explicit model pins (via route metadata) were receiving responses from the degraded fallback variant during the rolling prewarm window. The effect is intermittent: affected sessions often reconnect and resume pinned behavior after 2–8 minutes. Expected behavior: Pins should be respected during rollout; prewarm activity must not evict or clear tenant pin state. Severity rationale: Customer-visible quality regressions and billing anomalies with repeat occurrences.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy a staged canary with a rolling prewarm slope (example: 5% -> 25% over 30m) to prod us-west-2.
2) Ensure the target cohort includes tenants with explicit model version pins (e.g., tenant config: model_pin=gptx-neo-13b-q4).
3) Issue long-lived streaming requests from pinned tenants and keep-alive connection churn (simulate reconnects).
4) Observe routing decisions in request traces and look for fallbacks to compatibility variant during the prewarm ramp.
Expected result: Model pin persists for session lifetime.
Actual result: ~1-2% of sessions show pin lost and are routed to fallback variant for several minutes.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: prewarm-scheduler is interleaving probe/handshake traffic with tenant pin lease refresh and causing lease expiry on the orchestrator side under keep-alive churn.
Hypothesis B: edge-proxy header normalization on reconnect strips the pin-claim header during certain H2 stream reuse scenarios leading to controller interpreting session as unpinned.
Telemetry: observed concurrent kv lease refresh failures correlated with prewarm waves; 95th percentile kv latency increased from 45ms -> 380ms during slope window.
Partial repro: synthetic load reproduces 1.6% pin-loss when introducing reconnects at 30s intervals + prewarm slope active.
Related code area: prewarm-scheduler handshake logic and session-lease reaper in orchestrator v2.7.1.
Blocked: need a reproducer with full request traces and kvcache debug enabled (requires customer opt-in).

mitigation: Temporarily reduced prewarm slope from 5%->25% to 3%->15% and increased kvcache session lease TTL from default 30s to 90s for PaperTrail's dedicated pool; requested customer to postpone heavy reconnect experiments during canary windows.
next_steps:
1) Backport H2 header normalization fix to edge-proxy and add test for header preservation on H2 stream reuse (ENG-PR #1892).
2) Harden orchestrator session-lease refresh to tolerate prewarm-induced contention: implement jittered retry/backoff and bump default TTL.
3) Schedule a canary for the edge-proxy fix + orchestrator patch in staging, include synthetic reconnect load and prewarm slope replication.
4) Follow-up with PaperTrail AI after fix deployment and run a 24h validation window.
5) Postmortem doc and runbook updates to Prewarm Handshake Runbook.
